SMTO-TSK-0030 — That long-running command can't be changed anymore

GUID: 11243619-e505-4a67-9427-4ce81ffd5733
Slug: task-control-operation-ended
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The command you tried to keep running or end has already finished, been replaced, or its task is stopping. SMTO didn't apply your choice, and that doesn't prove the command stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and open the task. Look at the command's latest status and result in the task's activity. The command may have finished or been replaced since the buttons appeared.
  2. If the task shows Still running with Keep Running or Terminate buttons again, use those new buttons. Only the buttons for the command running now can change it.
  3. If you needed the command stopped and can't confirm that it did, select Stop on the task, or check the computer it was running on. A refused Terminate doesn't prove the command stopped on that computer.

What success looks like

  • The task's activity shows the command as finished or stopped, or shows your Keep Running or Terminate choice.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start the same command again until you know whether the first one is still running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Keep Running or Terminate control for a long-running command was rejected because the run is finished or stopping, this server no longer owns it, the operation ID changed, or the operation is not marked long_running.

What this means

  • Foreground controls find a terminal/unowned/stopping run, a different operation identity, or an operation not marked long_running. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Foreground controls find a terminal/unowned/stopping run, a different operation identity, or an operation not marked long_running.

How to diagnose it

  • Check current operation ID, owner and long-running status; control rejection does not prove remote work stopped.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the native run snapshot and compare the current operation's operation_id and long_running flag with the one the control targeted. A rejected control does not prove the remote process stopped; confirm the command's outcome from the activity result or on the target machine before issuing another control.
  • Refresh the current operation status and inspect its result. Use only controls still offered for that operation; a failed control does not prove that remote work stopped.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing results and ownership settle, and only currently offered controls are used.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
